# Independent audit: selected R4 menu and projected transport defects

Source: `candidate a9fd9b4c832ea48f`.

**Full PASS**, including the added exact hinge table. No repair identified.
The standalone verifier was rerun and passed all 2,719 exact checks.

## 1. Finite selection and capacity quantifiers

The joint constraints in (1) are linear in both the profile weights and
the transport. Fixed normal labels are retained, row barycenters are
physical barycenters, and target inequalities preserve unused capacity.
The transport variables lie in a compact bounded simplex, so their
projection is a compact convex polytope. Its convexity justifies testing
whether at least one extreme response profile escapes it; this is not a
minimax interchange and gives no quantitative Gamma bound on the escape.

Projected defects depend only on the source and target marginals, not on
the coupling. When their total masses agree the target capacity is full.
Expanding the quadratic displacement and using every row barycenter
then gives the precise energy identity (3). A positive moment defect
cannot be repaired by choosing a different martingale with those same
marginals.

## 2. Actual nine-cap menu and solved transport polytope

The inherited all-normal R4 theorem certifies each diagonal cap. Independent
base and continuous simplex permutations certify all nine caps at the same
source and raw mass. The strict full/empty traces and three proper zero-slice
traces give full regularity. In the unscaled barycentric margin convention,
the coarea is 3*(4V/3)=4V, so response balance is exactly the column-sum
condition (5).

The explicit base sums make the projected first moment of each facet
source proportional to (r_1-r_0,r_2-r_0). Equal facet masses force full
capacity and hence all row sums equal 1/3. Conversely, Birkhoff decomposition
is valid and finite. Every permutation of the three ell coordinates
preserves their common residue modulo 3 and their sum zero, so the displayed
inverse formulas give an actual unimodular base map. It takes the archived
physical, fixed-normal martingale to the corresponding permutation profile.
Mixtures then prove sufficiency on each entire continuous facet, with no
unproved boundary discretization.

Thus exactly six of the 27 extreme response profiles are transportable.
The other 21 fail already at first moments. This is selection information,
not a statement that a failed capacity test alone pays Gamma.

## 3. Quadratic defect and exact hinge slack

The invariant quadratic Q=z1^2-z1*z2+z2^2 is positive definite. Its total,
positive-slice, and zero-slice sums are respectively 165, 60, and 6. The
column constraints alone therefore give the profile-independent defect

    L[165-(60+8/3)/(40/93)]=(193/10)L.

This identity holds even at nontransportable menu weights; its displacement
interpretation is asserted only on the transportable subset. The separate
outer-vertex marginal contradiction is also correct and does not presume
existence of a transport.

For an affine-margin hinge, the Jensen remainder is the opposite-sign
positive part at the target. Zero deficit therefore preserves signs when
both marginals give no mass to the cutting plane. Zero deficits for every
menu hinge preserve the whole signature. Since the source density on each
signature cell is the constant W/beta, full-capacity transport then forces
W=beta almost everywhere. None of these zero-deficit premises follows from
criticality alone.

On an R4 facet the three equal subintervals capture every hinge breakpoint
and every profile jump. Midpoint integration is exact because the profile
is constant and the hinge affine on each open subinterval. The nine printed
fractions in (13) were checked by the verifier directly from the actual
margins. Base permutations only permute their rows; continuous-facet
permutations give the other facets. Convex combinations prove the uniform
strict lower bound 1129L/720 for all nine hinges and every transportable
response matrix. This correctly obstructs the proposed Jensen-equality
closure within this menu.

The source retains all necessary limits of scope: an actual above-target
calibration, a finite selected-menu alternative, and a concrete failure of
projected stationarity. No attained bad-minimum or general OC conclusion
is inferred.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
